items.title: Front door latch freezing in "open position" in cold weather
items.body:
I live in Canada in a recently renovated house with tight building envelope. I've noticed in cold weather, roughly -15C (5F) or below, the front door latch (will sometimes get stuck in the open position (i.e. the 'bolt' will not come out of its hole, or will only partially return to the 'closed' position), making it impossible to shut the door without manually pulling it out with a pair of pliers.

I've opened up the handle and there is a fair amount of condensation on the latch mechanism. I suspect that when I open the door, the cold end of the bolt freezes some of the water in the interior of the mechanism. The two screw holes in Figure 3 have big gaps in them so warm house air is free to go into the bore of the door.

I also notice that the exterior 'thumb latch' handle (Figure 4) seems more prone to not returning to its neutral position than the interior handle (Figure 3). I notice sometimes a bit (or a lot!) of frost accumulating in the there opening, which probably doesn't help.

Indoor humidity is 40-45% (Figure 2). I realize this is a bit higher than recommended, but its tricky to get it into the 30's. We run the HRV ~40 minutes/hr (I'm not sure the humidistat function works on our thermostat/controller).

Figure 1

Figure 2

Figure 3

Figure 4

My question

How can I help prevent the latch from icing up in cold weather? I'm especially looking for solutions at the door. I know reducing humidity will help but super low humidity will cause me other problems with wood, instruments, etc. However, if you think I'm being an idiot and just need to turn my house into a desert, that's a valid answer too.

I've considered:

  • a waterproof lubricant for the door latch, but not sure what to use - I tried graphite lube but it just made a mess (as you can see in the pictures)
  • sealing the holes in the door latch to reduce warm air flow into the door bore.
  • replacing the exterior thumb-handle with a regular handle.

items.title: Internal latch plate stuck in latch bore?
items.body:
I am trying to replace my interior door knobs and am really struggling to remove the latch in my bathroom door. The latch plate (which goes into the latch bore) was painted over so I assumed that’s why it wouldn't budge.

I was able to disassemble the latch while it was still in the door and remove it that way, however the latch plate is still stuck in the latch bore and possibly still a part of the latch. I’ve tried to remove it with pliers but have just managed to bend or break everything I can manage to grab onto.

Is there any way to remove this?

Is it possible that this is built into or glued into the door?

Am I going to need to replace the whole door?

items.title: Door latch can be forced out of strike plate without turning handle
items.body:
We have recently bought an adhesive door lock for my 3 year old's bedroom to stop her getting out of her room at night. However, we have discovered she is able to yank the door handle with enough force that it opens regardless (even though the door is latched and the adhesive lock we've stuck on does not allow the handle to be turned).

To try and prevent the latch giving way so easily, I have tried to make some adjustments to the door strike plate:

  • Added a couple of washers behind each screw which is behind the plate. This helped the plate stick out a bit more from the doorframe, prior to this it was quite deeply set.
  • Added more washers behind the edge of the plate (visible in image) as the plate was tilting inwards.
  • Used some pliers to try and flatten the inside of the plate to prevent the latch slipping out so easily.

However, none of these seem to have prevented the issue and I'm not sure what to try next without resorting to something more involved, such as installing a bolt lock into the door frame or something.

Is there anything else I could try?

items.title: Latch locks when door handle pulled down
items.body: Had our front door repainted (simply took off hinges and then replaced). Now, when you open the door by pulling handle down the latch stays stuck such that you can't open it from the other side. You have to pull up on the handle to release it and then the door can again be opened. Any thoughts?

items.title: Whirlpool Over the Range Microwave suddenly lost power after messing with door switch
items.body:
My 3 year old Whirlpool Over the Range Microwave was sometimes not detecting the door as closed (when it was) when I tried to running it. All it took was a couple of opens and closes and eventually it would register.

It's been like that for a several months and I never really did anything about it. However, the other day I got curious and thought it might be a sticky door latch, so as I kept the microwave door open I stuck a wooden pick in one of the door slots (top one) and I assume this activated the switch on the top only (heard it click in). I then realized my microwave now had no power at all (screen was completely off).

Any idea what could've happened and went wrong?

I am almost completely certain that the act of me sticking the pick in the top door latch is when the microwave went completely dead.

items.title: Key stuck halfway in door lock
items.body: My bedroom door has a lock on it and the key is stuck between a 90 degree turn and the top (pictures below). The weird thing is that when I turn it counter clockwise it moves the latch bolt just a tiny amount and then gets stuck again. I’ve tried turning the handle while attempting to unlock or remove the key and everything else I could think of. I really don’t want to have to call my landlord just for a locksmith to come and fix it in 10 seconds because of something stupid I couldn’t think of. I’ve never seen a key/lock get stuck like this before so all help is appreciated, thank you!

items.title: Garage door opener get stuck sometimes
items.body:
My garage door opener get stuck sometimes, it gives the sound it is going to close the garage door then it rolls back a little then stops.

Another push to the remote and same thing happens, it tries to move forward then backward a little then stops.

I'm not sure, should I clean the roller chain (what to use to clean it?), replace it, or does the problem in the opener engine, need to be replaced?

When I try to disconnect the door from the latch and close it manually, the problem is still there - it moves forward a little then backward then stops even though door is not connected.

items.title: Broken washing machine latch
items.body:
The latch on my washing machine is broken and consequently my washing machine doesn't close or work.
I ordered a replacement part from Amazon, but while I wait for that to arrive I was looking at the locking mechanism. It seems like the bolt that holds the latch in place is stuck in the locked position and that may be why the tip of the latch broke off (since the tip is still in the machine).

Following generic instructions on Youtube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3dLhBoBC1DM,
I should be able to take off the boot and manually unlock the mechanism.

My question to people who may be more familiar with the situation is: is the fact that the locking mechanism is in the up position a sign that the mechanism itself is likely broken or is this actual the default position for the bolt?
What I don't want to do is reset the machine, give it a run and the lock gets stuck with the new latch and I can't open the door of the washing machine to do anything.
